context: Post-epidemic eosinophilia myalgia syndrome associated with L-Tryptophan Eosinophilia–myalgia syndrome (EMS) is characterized by subacute onset of myalgias and peripheral eosinophilia, followed by chronic neuropathy and skin induration. An epidemic of EMS in 1989 was linked to L-tryptophan consumption originating from a single source. Following the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) ban on the sale of L-tryptophan, the incidence of EMS declined rapidly.
target: Moreover, no new cases have been published since the FDA ban was lifted in 2005.
